persona.role: PhD student and machine learning researcher
current_work: Investigating calibration robustness to noisy target prevalence estimates
Comparing calibration methods under controlled prevalence perturbations
Maintaining research code and experiment infrastructure
Preparing a focused pilot analysis for a potential follow-up study
priorities: Complete a standardized method-by-noise comparison using the existing dataset
Determine whether prevalence-estimation noise changes relative method behavior
Keep the pilot analysis reproducible and bounded
Decide whether the observed pattern is strong enough to justify a broader study

circumstances: The researcher formalizes the small method-by-noise comparison from Day 26 and runs it with the standardized metric configuration. The results show that the methods differ at low noise, but their ranking becomes less distinct at moderate noise. At the highest noise level, uncertainty intervals overlap substantially. The researcher checks whether the result is driven by one class, repeats the analysis with class-conditional reporting, and finds that the aggregate ranking hides a reversal for one low-frequency class. They begin drafting a figure and a short internal results note. A literature search for a directly comparable study finds related work but no exact match. The researcher ends the day with a decision point rather than adding another dataset.

activities.title: Run and analyze the standardized method-by-noise comparison
activities.summary: The researcher validated the fixed comparison, ran the existing methods under standardized metrics and prevalence-noise levels, and compared aggregate rankings and uncertainty intervals. Method differences were clearer at low noise but became less distinct as noise increased.
activities.context: Direct continuation of the controlled comparison planned on Day 26.

activities.title: Compare the result with related work and inspect class-level reversal
activities.summary: The researcher searched for closely related method comparisons, found related but not identical work, and rechecked a class-conditional reversal that was obscured by aggregate rankings at high noise.
activities.context: Interpreting the standardized comparison before expanding the study.

activities.title: Document preliminary results and limitations
activities.summary: The researcher wrote an internal results note emphasizing the reduced separation between methods at higher noise and the uncertainty around the class-level reversal.
activities.context: Capturing the current evidence before deciding on further experiments.

activities.title: Prepare a figure and define a stopping decision
activities.summary: The researcher drafted a figure showing aggregate and class-conditional behavior, checked plotting documentation, and wrote criteria for deciding whether the pilot should expand or stop.
activities.context: Turning the pilot output into interpretable evidence and an explicit next decision.

key_observations: The standardized comparison shows that method differences are more distinct at low prevalence-estimation noise and become harder to separate as noise increases.
At high noise, uncertainty intervals overlap substantially, so the apparent method ranking is not strong evidence of a reliable ordering.
Class-conditional reporting reveals a reversal for one low-frequency class that is hidden by aggregate metrics.
Related literature is relevant but does not provide an exact methodological match, leaving room for a carefully scoped contribution.
The researcher has now written explicit criteria for deciding whether to expand the pilot rather than allowing the experiment matrix to grow automatically.
priority_alignment: The planned standardized comparison was completed without adding another dataset.
The analysis preserved class-conditional reporting instead of relying only on aggregate rankings.
The next decision is now based on predefined evidence rather than enthusiasm for a surprising result.
important_uncertainty: The high-noise method ranking is weak because the uncertainty intervals overlap.
The class-level reversal may still be sensitive to the chosen dataset and seed.
It is not yet clear whether the observed interaction is strong enough to justify a broader study.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Review the pilot against the written stopping criteria and, if the evidence passes, run one carefully specified confirmation seed before considering a second dataset.

primary_action.title: Apply the pilot stopping criteria
primary_action.reason: The comparison now has enough structure to decide whether another confirmation run is justified, but the evidence does not yet support broad expansion.

secondary_action.title: Keep aggregate and class-level results together
secondary_action.reason: The aggregate ranking hides an important class-level reversal, so future evaluation should preserve both views.

things_not_to_do: Do not claim a stable method ranking at high noise when uncertainty intervals overlap.
Do not add a second dataset before applying the existing stopping criteria.
Do not discard the class-level reversal because the aggregate metric looks cleaner.
Do not keep iterating on the figure as a substitute for deciding whether the evidence warrants another experiment.
